parts.text: In this experiment, you will determine the spring constant k of a spring. Carry out the following instructions, referring to Fig. 1.1. Fig. 1.1

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) The metre rule is fixed in position close to the spring. Do not change the position of the metre rule.

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Record in Table 1.1 the value of the length of the spring l 0 when the load L is 0.00 N. [1]

ms.label: 1(a)(ii)
ms.text:
l = difference between the two scale readings recorded in the table
0

parts.label: iii
parts.text: (iii) • Place a load of 0.20 N on the spring. Record in Table 1.1 the new length l of the spring. • Use the equation e = ( l – l 0 ) to calculate the extension e of the spring. Record the value of e in the table. • Repeat the procedure using loads of 0.40 N, 0.60 N, 0.80 N and 1.00 N. Record all the readings and results in the table. Table 1.1 L / N l / mm e / mm 0.00 0 0.20 0.40 0.60 0.80 1.00 [2]

ms.label: 1(a)(iii)
ms.text:
increasing values of l in table
correct e values

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) Plot a graph of L / N ( y -axis) against e / mm ( x -axis). [4]

ms.label: 1(b)
ms.text:
graph:
axes correctly labelled and right way round
suitable scales
all plots correct to ½ small square
good line judgement, thin, continuous line

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) Determine the gradient G of the graph. Show clearly on the graph how you obtained the necessary information. G = ...........................................................[2]

ms.label: 1(c)
ms.text:
triangle method used and seen on graph
at least half of candidate’s line used

parts.label: d
parts.text: (d) The gradient G is numerically equal to the spring constant k . Write down a value for k to a suitable number of significant figures for this experiment. k = ............................................... N / mm [1]

ms.label: 1(d)
ms.text: k correct to 2 or 3 significant figures
